It’s the case of Jesus Herrada (Burgos Burpellet BH), who is set to retire at the end of La Vuelta 26. Today’s course echoes the first of his three La Vuelta victories, in 2019: the stage started in Mora de Rubielos (km 122 on today’s course) and finished in Ares del Maestrat (around 40 kilometres north of today’s start).
“To be honest, it’s a marvellous place", the Spanish vetera said at the start. "My brother José and I started coming here quite a few years ago to train, and I really loved it for training. It’s at 1,700 metres, in Spain’s highest village, and it’s practically been my second home for many years – I’ve held all my training camps there over the years. Because of the quality of the place, the people… everything. I wouldn’t change it for anything. The finish is very tough. The stage is short, but it involves a lot of elevation gain, constantly climbing with passes of 6–7 kilometres. And above all, the final climb has some very steep sections, at over 10%. The finish is at almost 2,000 metres.
